title: Georgia AG and GBI return roughly $151,000 in crypto stolen from Columbia County scam victim
date_note: The page gives only its publication day; it describes the action as taking place today.
org: Georgia Attorney General's Office / Georgia Bureau of Investigation
geo_basis: county named in the source; centre of county used, victim's city not stated
summary: Valdosta Today reports that Georgia's Attorney General and the Georgia Bureau of Investigation traced and seized a portion of stolen crypto, totaling roughly $151,000, taken from a Columbia County woman. The victim was contacted through LinkedIn and persuaded to join a "crypto investment" through a fraudulent app. The funds were returned to her.
plain: Georgia authorities say they traced and recovered roughly $151,000 in crypto taken from a woman who was lured into a fake investment app after a LinkedIn contact.
exec: Georgia authorities report recovering roughly $151,000 in crypto from a fake-app investment scam that began on LinkedIn.
impact: Roughly $151,000 in stolen crypto was traced, seized and returned, per the report.

evidence.quote: worked to trace and seize a portion of the stolen crypto – totaling roughly $151,000.

validation.note: One publisher (Valdosta Today) relaying the Attorney General's announcement; the original release was not read.
